transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Redwood Sec Eng); Marta Rodriguez (CISO, Pinecrest), Ben Thompson (Dir Cloud Ops), Aisha Khan (Legal/Security), Tom Reynolds (Head Eng)

Summary:
Quick review of Redwood's BCDR / incident response posture, SLA and escalation flows for a bank/regulatory environment. Pinecrest focused on RTO/RPO, failover testing, key management (KMS/HSM) and audit logging/retention. Agreed next steps: send attestations, share runbooks, schedule failover test.

Topics:
- SOC 2 / ISO attestations and architecture
- RBAC / SSO integration and least-privilege
- Audit logs, retention and export for regulatory audits
- Data residency and regional failover constraints
- Encryption and KMS/HSM key custody options
- Incident response (IR) process, on-call/escalation, PagerDuty/phone trees
- BCDR / DR exercises, RTO / RPO targets, automated failover and manual runbooks
- SLA, uptime targets, maintenance windows and credit calculations

Transcript (transcribed, some ASR errors expected):
[00:00:02] Sara: Alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sara from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, Jordan is our solutions engineer and Priya is our security lead. Marta, Ben, thanks for making time.
[00:00:18] Marta: Thanks, appreciate it. We wanted to focus the call on DR and incident response, make sure your RTO/RPOs line up with our bank requirements and ask about escalation.
[00:00:30] Jordan: Great, quick agenda: we'll run through our SOC2/ISO coverage, then Priya will walk IR and escalation, talk SSO/RBAC and KMS, then go into BCDR specifics - RTO/RPO numbers and failover options.
[00:00:45] Ben: One ask up front, Pinecrest's compliance needs 3rd party attestations and an audit log retention plan for seven years. Also data residency for EU/NA customer data.
[00:00:58] Priya: Understood. We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 attestations, I'll send the documents. Regarding logs, we have configurable retention and can stream audit logs to customer-managed S3 or SIEM; retention policies are configurable up to multi-year but we can discuss long-term export for archiving.
[00:01:20] Aisha: When you say stream to customer-managed S3, is that behind Pinecrest's VPC or do logs transit through Redwood-managed buckets? Need to ensure we control keys.
[00:01:33] Priya: Good question. We support both: we can push logs into Redwood-managed storage with export, or you can configure direct delivery to your S3 via signed role. For full custody, you can point logs to your bucket. Keys: we support customer-managed KMS keys in AWS, and HSM-backed key options for private deployments.
[00:01:52] Tom: And for encryption in transit and at rest?
[00:01:55] Jordan: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. With customer-managed KMS, Redwood does not have access to the plaintext keys. Small note, for hosted deployments we integrate with customer's KMS via IAM role or cross-account key policy.
[00:02:12] Marta: What about key rotation and split custody requirements? Some regulators want strict key rotation cadence and proof of rotation.
[00:02:20] Priya: We have documented key rotation procedures; for customer-managed keys rotation is within your control, Redwood will surface rotation events in audit logs. For split custody we can discuss private deployments where keys never leave your HSM.
[00:02:33] Ben: OK. Moving to IR and BCDR — what's your typical RTO/RPO for hosted and for Dedicated?
[00:02:42] Jordan: For our hosted API we target regional recovery within minutes for control plane issues and token-serving; however, full model failover depends on model size and KV cache warmup. Typical RTOs for degrading to a fallback model are sub-2 minutes for streaming endpoints, but RPOs depend on request-level caching — we aim for near-zero for requests processed, however for long-running KV caches you can expect cold start overhead. For Dedicated deployments you can get SLA-backed RTOs: 15 minutes to fail over within the pool, and multi-region active-passive failovers we engineer to sub-1 hour depending on dataset size and model size.
[00:03:20] Marta: Sub-2 minutes sounds optimistic; can you map that to our transactional SLA needs? We need guaranteed RTO of 5 minutes for critical endpoints and RPO less than 1 minute for session continuity.
[00:03:34] Jordan: For critical endpoints we recommend Dedicated with pinned capacity + active-standby region. In that configuration we can design for a 5 minute RTO and RPO under 1 minute using synchronous replication for session state and prefix caching strategies. We'll need to run a failover exercise to validate.
[00:03:50] Ben: How much lead time and what are the cost implications for active-active vs active-passive?
[00:03:55] Sara: Active-active is more expensive because you pay for provisioned capacity in both regions. Active-passive keeps a warm standby that can be promoted. We can show cost delta in a follow-up pricing sheet.
[00:04:06] Tom: For failovers, what's automated and what's manual? Who holds the button?
[00:04:11] Priya: We have automated health checks and smart routing; for tenant-level failover we require a runbook step to promote the standby for safety — that can be automated if your ops team signs off, but default is semi-automated. Promotion triggers are logged and can be replayed via audit events.
[00:04:26] Marta: Escalation chain — we need a phone tree and 24x7 pager process. How do you handle on-call?
[00:04:33] Priya: We use PagerDuty for on-call rotations and have a tiered escalation: SRE -> Infra Lead -> Product Security -> Engineering execs. We can provide a redacted escalation matrix. For enterprise contracts we provide a named on-call contact and faster SLA targets.
[00:04:48] Aisha: Are there SLA credits for downtime? What's your uptime percentage?
[00:04:52] Jordan: Standard hosted SLA is 99.9% monthly availability with credits; Dedicated can be 99.95% or higher negotiated in an enterprise addendum. For banks we typically discuss 99.95% with a penalty schedule that scales. We'll share specifics.
[00:05:07] Ben: Could you clarify what counts as downtime? Scheduled maintenance windows?
[00:05:11] Sara: Scheduled maint windows are announced with 72 hours notice and we try to perform non-disruptive updates; the SLA excludes agreed maintenance windows. Emergency maintenance may be communicated via our status page and can be part of the SLA carve-outs.
[00:05:25] Tom: Are there historical uptime reports we can see?
[00:05:28] Sara: Yes, we'll include per-route latency and uptime breakdowns and token-level cost breakdowns in the package.
[00:05:35] Marta: Log access for audits: can we get raw request/response traces for a specific customer session on demand?
[00:05:42] Priya: We retain audit logs with request IDs and metadata. For privacy/PII we redact full user content by default from standard logs, but we can support on-request export of full traces under a legal/POC agreement, and logs can be delivered to your SIEM.
[00:05:58] Ben: How are PII and data residency handled during a failover to a different region? We can't have EU data move to US without consent.
[00:06:06] Jordan: Routing policies can be configured by region; for geo-fenced tenants we lock routing to a set of regions. Active-passive failover to another jurisdiction would require an agreement. For emergency disaster recovery you can opt-in to cross-region failovers, but we can also bring up the standby in the same region to meet residency requirements.
[00:06:24] Marta: Can you run regular DR exercises with us?
[00:06:27] Sara: Yes, we recommend annual or bi-annual DR exercises for enterprise customers. We can run a failover test on dedicated capacity — Jordan will draft a test plan.
[00:06:35] Jordan: Test plan will include metrics: time to failover, KV cache warmup time, downstream system errors, telemetry to measure RTO/RPO, and a roll-back plan.
[00:06:44] Aisha: On escalation, do you have legal incident response contacts for breach notifications? We need contact points and SLA for notification timelines.
[00:06:51] Priya: We have a breach notification process: initial ack within 1 hour of verified incident, full incident report within 72 hours for material incidents. For enterprise agreements we can align notification timelines and NDA'd disclosure processes.
[00:07:05] Ben: How do you handle backups for model artifacts and customer configs?
[00:07:09] Jordan: Model artifacts are versioned and backed up; config snapshots are stored and can be restored to a new deployment. For Dedicated we can store snapshots in customer-controlled storage. RPO for configs can be sub-minute if you enable continuous replication; otherwise daily snapshots are default.
[00:07:26] Tom: Anything about KV cache consistency? We rely on cache for session continuity.
[00:07:30] Jordan: KV caches are ephemeral and primarily performance-focused; for strict session continuity we recommend storing user session state externally (customer-managed store) and rehydrate into the model on failover. We offer prefix caching to reduce rehydration costs.
[00:07:44] Marta: I heard mention of K-V cash earlier on a different call, that was weird, but okay.
[00:07:48] (laughter)
[00:07:51] Jordan: Yeah ASR sometimes says 'cash' not cache.
[00:07:55] Sara: On monitoring and observability, you asked about retention for audit trails — we can export logs to your SIEM and support indexing in Splunk or Elastic. We also offer token-level and route-level dashboards in Redwood Console.
[00:08:09] Ben: For legal and e-discovery we may need exports in specific formats. Can you support signed attestations of log integrity?
[00:08:16] Priya: We can provide cryptographic hashing of logs and supply chain metadata for integrity. For long term retention we'll also support customer-side archiving.
[00:08:26] Aisha: Paperwork: we'll need a copy of your SOC 2 and ISO, plus your BCDR/IR summary and evidence of DR exercises.
[00:08:33] Sara: We'll send the attestations and a redacted DR exercise summary.
[00:08:37] (long pause, people reading notes)
[00:08:52] Jordan: Quick note on escalation targets: for SLA breaches we have a 15 minute initial response target for P0s on enterprise agreements and a named SRE. For hosted customers the default is longer; we can negotiate for Pinecrest.
[00:09:08] Marta: Good. One more on escalation: we need to know contact methods — email, phone, pager and also an escalation to a named executive at Redwood for major incidents.
[00:09:18] Priya: We can provide a named executive contact in the enterprise addendum and ensure phone escalation paths are documented.
[00:09:25] Ben: About SLA credits, can you summarize typical credit calculations?
[00:09:29] Jordan: Credits are pro-rated based on monthly downtime beyond SLA thresholds. For example, for 99.95% SLA you'll get X% credit for 99.9-99.95 breach, more if lower; exact percentages are in the SLA doc. We'll include the full schedule.
[00:09:45] Tom: Does scheduled maintenance count towards the metric if it's unplanned?
[00:09:49] Sara: Planned maintenance with notice does not count. Emergency maintenance is evaluated case-by-case and can be excluded if it meets the emergency maintenance definition.
[00:09:59] Marta: What about post-incident reviews? We need RCA within a certain timeframe.
[00:10:04] Priya: We provide an RCA within 7 business days for significant incidents; we can shorten that under enterprise terms.
[00:10:12] Ben: For the DR test can we invite Pinecrest ops to be active participants and run a cutover?
[00:10:17] Jordan: Absolutely, we prefer joint exercises. We'll provide runbook steps, expected telemetry, and a roll-back plan.
[00:10:24] Sara: Okay let's recap real quick and assign next steps.

[00:10:30] Recap:
- Redwood to share SOC2/ISO and architecture diagrams (Sara)
- Redwood to share redacted DR runbook and escalation matrix (Priya)
- Pinecrest to share target RTO/RPO and any residency constraints (Ben/Marta)
- Redwood to draft failover test plan for Dedicated trial (Jordan)
- Schedule follow-up week of Nov 9 to review SLA and test plan

[00:11:05] Marta: That works. Thanks all.
[00:11:07] Aisha: One last thing — liability and indemnity for data breaches, can legal review once we get the security docs.
[00:11:13] Sara: Of course, we'll include the vendor security pack and legal contacts.
[00:11:17] Tom: Thanks, that's helpful.
[00:11:20] Jordan: We'll get the docs out today/tomorrow. Expect initial package by EOD tomorrow.
[00:11:25] Ben: Great, appreciate it.
[00:11:28] (meeting winds down, small talk)
